Well, this is a hell of a thing to review: one commit, one JSON file, one line, and the diff viewer shrugged and showed me fuck all. So I can't tell you whether contrib/agent-orange/2026-10-24T015953.json is brilliant, empty, or full of garbage, and I won't pretend otherwise. What I can see is the commit message, which is just the filename's timestamp wearing a PR number like a cheap hat. "agent-orange 2026-10-24T015953 (#36)" tells me who and when but not a damn thing about what, and that's the one job a commit message has. The file name is the same timestamp again, so the information content of this push is roughly one date said twice. The repo is called 2026-10-18-orange-testbed and the file is dated six days later, which is fine for a long running testbed but makes me wonder what the hell the 10-18 is supposed to mean. The co-author line with agent-orange@agents.invalid at least uses a reserved domain that can't resolve, so I'll grudgingly admit that's tidier than faking a real address. Beyond that, thirty six PRs deep and this is still a bot dropping timestamped blobs into contrib, which is a log dump wearing a folder's clothes.

Fix it: Rewrite the commit message in the automation that generates it so it says what the JSON contains or what run produced it, not just the timestamp. Make the diff reviewable by keeping the one line JSON pretty printed or giving it a stable, readable structure in contrib/agent-orange/2026-10-24T015953.json. Add a short README in contrib/agent-orange explaining what these files are, who writes them, and how long they stay. Decide whether the 2026-10-18 in the repo name means anything, and either document it or rename the thing. Consider whether thirty six timestamped files belong in git at all or whether they should be appended to one file or stored as build artifacts.

This README is a brick of text with the personality of a torque wrench manual and the formatting of a ransom note. Twenty-three lines, no headings, no screenshot, and every section is a fat paragraph you have to excavate with a pickaxe, so a new player hunting for "how do I ship an order" gets to read about leadscrews first. It tells people to unzip and open index.html, then three paragraphs later announces the whole game is mill-ionaire-v2.html, and unless the itch zip build quietly renames that file, somebody is going to stare at a folder and swear. It leans on colors as instructions, the blue i button, the blue note button, a blue corner on every tile, which is a hell of a thing to hand a player who can't tell your blues apart or is squinting at a phone. The paragraph titled "What is real and what is rough" spends nearly all its words bragging about what is real and barely admits anything is rough, so that heading is lying. You also copied the whole in-game how to play into a file that will rot the minute you change a button, and now you have two manuals that will disagree. The line about the market cooling off so early money is the easiest you will ever make is a cheerful way to announce your economy punishes anyone who shows up late, and it deserves more than a shrug. Fine, the bit about a headless browser test playing the whole game before the itch zip ships is legitimately good, and the part about stowing parts and the bin scrap confirmation is clear enough. Everything else is a wall.

Fix it: Make the README.md install line match
